correctness.rationale: PASS: The prescribed global-max norm relaxation for rows a1=(1,0), a2=√(1−τ²)(ρ,√(1−ρ²)), τ,ρ∈(0,1), is ω1=1 and ω2=1+τ. In exact arithmetic U=I−uuᵀ, V=I−vvᵀ, W=I−(1+τ)vvᵀ. Enumerating four iid uniform two-step words gives second-moment matrices B_Z=1/4[U(U²+Z²)U+Z(U²+Z²)Z], and difference D=B_W−B_V. Direct exact product yields tr D=τ²(τ²+2s²)/4>0, det D=(ρ²s²τ²/16)[τ⁴+τ(τ+2)s²−1], s²=1−ρ². A symmetric 2×2 matrix with positive trace has negative eigenvalue iff determinant<0; equality or reverse means positive semidefinite, proving the all-initial-errors classification including equality and strict worse directions. One-step difference τ²(eᵀQe)/2 is nonnegative for every e and strictly positive unless Qe=0; the source correctly says 'never better', not strictly worse for all. Independently enumerated exact rational four-word matrices for τ=s=3/5, ρ=4/5, e=(0,1) to get Eunit=1681/2500, Erel=10297/15625, difference −837/62500. The τ0 quartic derivative is positive, so unique threshold root. No claim beyond two steps or all initialization improvement.
